This is the Machine Learning Practical (MLP) coursework framework used in an introductory deep-learning course. It provides a NumPy-based neural network library (`mlp` package) for building and training neural networks from scratch. Multiple core modules have been left unimplemented and must be completed so that all tests pass.

Your working directory is `/workspace`. The project code is already present at `/workspace/mlp/`.

Implement the following modules:

The following modules need to be implemented or substantially built out:

layers (`mlp/layers.py`): Neural network layer implementations including affine (fully connected) transformations, activation functions (sigmoid, ReLU, leaky ReLU, ELU, SELU, tanh, softmax), radial basis function projections, dropout, reshape, batch normalization, and 2D convolution. In addition to the forward/backward passes, this task now also hollows constructor and parameter-interface logic for the affine, batch-normalization, convolution, RBF, dropout, leaky-ReLU, ELU, SELU, and reshape layers where those interfaces are exercised by the tests. (~52 functions / interfaces to implement)

errors (`mlp/errors.py`): Scalar error (loss) functions used to train models, including sum-of-squared-differences, binary cross-entropy, binary cross-entropy with sigmoid, multi-class cross-entropy, and cross-entropy with softmax. Each error function requires both a forward evaluation method and a gradient method. (~10 functions to implement)

learning_rules (`mlp/learning_rules.py`): Gradient-based parameter update rules including base gradient-descent parameter initialisation/update handling, constructor-level hyperparameter validation/storage, momentum SGD, RMSProp, and Adam. The adaptive rules must also initialise and reset their optimizer state in addition to performing in-place parameter updates, and Momentum now also hollows its reset path. (~15 functions / interfaces to implement)

models (`mlp/models.py`): The single-layer and multi-layer model classes which store their wrapped layer(s), proxy wrapped-layer parameters/gradients, orchestrate forward propagation through a sequence of layers, expose a flattened `params` view over all parameterised layers, and compute gradients with respect to all model parameters via backpropagation. (~8 functions / interfaces to implement)

optimisers (`mlp/optimisers.py`): The training-loop optimiser that wires models, error functions, learning rules, and datasets together. It must initialise the learning rule from model parameters, execute batched training epochs, evaluate monitor metrics, aggregate per-epoch statistics, log them, and return full run statistics. (~6 functions / interfaces to implement)

The tests also depend on these signatures and entry points:

The following functions are called directly by the test suite. You must implement them with these exact signatures:

Layers (`mlp/layers.py`):
`AffineLayer.__init__(self, input_dim, output_dim, weights_initialiser=..., biases_initialiser=..., weights_penalty=None, biases_penalty=None)` — Initialises layer dimensions, parameter arrays, and optional penalties.
`AffineLayer.fprop(self, inputs)` — Forward pass computing `W @ x + b` for the affine transformation.
`AffineLayer.bprop(self, inputs, outputs, grads_wrt_outputs)` — Backward pass computing gradients with respect to inputs.
`AffineLayer.grads_wrt_params(self, inputs, grads_wrt_outputs)` — Returns `[grads_wrt_weights, grads_wrt_biases]`. Includes penalty gradients if set.
`AffineLayer.params_penalty(self)` — Returns scalar parameter-dependent penalty (0 if no penalties set).
`AffineLayer.params` — Getter/setter pair over `[weights, biases]`.
`SigmoidLayer.fprop(self, inputs)` — Applies the logistic sigmoid element-wise.
`SigmoidLayer.bprop(self, inputs, outputs, grads_wrt_outputs)` — Backward pass for sigmoid.
`ReluLayer.fprop(self, inputs)` — Applies element-wise ReLU.
`ReluLayer.bprop(self, inputs, outputs, grads_wrt_outputs)` — Backward pass for ReLU.
`LeakyReluLayer.__init__(self, alpha=0.01)` — Stores the negative-slope coefficient.
`LeakyReluLayer.fprop(self, inputs)` — Forward pass applying leaky ReLU activation with `self.alpha` slope for negative inputs.
`LeakyReluLayer.bprop(self, inputs, outputs, grads_wrt_outputs)` — Backward pass for leaky ReLU.
`ELULayer.__init__(self, alpha=1.0)` — Stores the ELU alpha parameter.
`ELULayer.fprop(self, inputs)` — Forward pass applying ELU activation with `self.alpha` parameter.
`ELULayer.bprop(self, inputs, outputs, grads_wrt_outputs)` — Backward pass for ELU.
`SELULayer.__init__(self)` — Initialises `self.alpha`, `self.lamda`, and the delegated `self.elu` layer.
`SELULayer.fprop(self, inputs)` — Forward pass applying SELU activation using `self.alpha` and `self.lamda` constants.
`SELULayer.bprop(self, inputs, outputs, grads_wrt_outputs)` — Backward pass for SELU.
`TanhLayer.fprop(self, inputs)` — Applies element-wise hyperbolic tangent.
`TanhLayer.bprop(self, inputs, outputs, grads_wrt_outputs)` — Backward pass for tanh.
`SoftmaxLayer.fprop(self, inputs)` — Applies softmax to produce probability distribution per sample.
`SoftmaxLayer.bprop(self, inputs, outputs, grads_wrt_outputs)` — Backward pass for softmax.
`RadialBasisFunctionLayer.__init__(self, grid_dim, intervals=[[0., 1.]])` — Builds the RBF centre grid and per-dimension scales.
`RadialBasisFunctionLayer.fprop(self, inputs)` — Projects inputs to grid of radial basis functions.
`RadialBasisFunctionLayer.bprop(self, inputs, outputs, grads_wrt_outputs)` — Backward pass for RBF layer.
`DropoutLayer.__init__(self, rng=None, incl_prob=0.5, share_across_batch=True)` — Stores dropout configuration and RNG.
`DropoutLayer.fprop(self, inputs, stochastic=True)` — Stochastically zeros inputs (if stochastic) or scales by inclusion probability (if deterministic).
`DropoutLayer.bprop(self, inputs, outputs, grads_wrt_outputs)` — Backward pass masking gradients consistently with the forward pass.
`ReshapeLayer.__init__(self, output_shape=None)` — Stores the per-example output shape, defaulting to flattening each input.
`ReshapeLayer.fprop(self, inputs)` — Reshapes each batch element to `self.output_shape`.
`ReshapeLayer.bprop(self, inputs, outputs, grads_wrt_outputs)` — Restores gradients to the original input shape.
`BatchNormalizationLayer.__init__(self, input_dim, rng=None)` — Initialises `gamma`, `beta`, `epsilon`, and caches for batch normalisation.
`BatchNormalizationLayer.fprop(self, inputs, stochastic=True)` — Forward pass of batch normalization layer, normalizing inputs and applying learnable scale/shift.
`BatchNormalizationLayer.bprop(self, inputs, outputs, grads_wrt_outputs)` — Backward pass computing gradients with respect to layer inputs.
`BatchNormalizationLayer.grads_wrt_params(self, inputs, grads_wrt_outputs)` — Returns `[grads_wrt_gamma, grads_wrt_beta]`.
`BatchNormalizationLayer.params_penalty(self)` — Returns zero for this layer’s parameter-dependent penalty term.
`BatchNormalizationLayer.params` — Getter/setter pair over `[gamma, beta]`.
`ConvolutionalLayer.__init__(self, num_input_channels, num_output_channels, input_dim_1, input_dim_2, kernel_dim_1, kernel_dim_2, kernels_init=..., biases_init=..., kernels_penalty=None, biases_penalty=None)` — Initialises convolution shapes, parameter arrays, and optional penalties.
`ConvolutionalLayer.fprop(self, inputs)` — Forward pass of 2D convolution. Inputs shape: `(batch, C_in, H, W)`. Output shape: `(batch, C_out, H-kH+1, W-kW+1)`.
`ConvolutionalLayer.bprop(self, inputs, outputs, grads_wrt_outputs)` — Backward pass computing gradients with respect to inputs.
`ConvolutionalLayer.grads_wrt_params(self, inputs, grads_wrt_outputs)` — Returns `[grads_wrt_kernels, grads_wrt_biases]`.
`ConvolutionalLayer.params_penalty(self)` — Returns scalar penalty aggregated over kernels and biases.
`ConvolutionalLayer.params` — Getter/setter pair over `[kernels, biases]`.

Error functions (`mlp/errors.py`):
`SumOfSquaredDiffsError.__call__(self, outputs, targets)` — Returns scalar mean sum of squared differences.
`SumOfSquaredDiffsError.grad(self, outputs, targets)` — Returns gradient of error with respect to outputs.
`CrossEntropyError.__call__(self, outputs, targets)` — Returns scalar multi-class cross-entropy.
`CrossEntropyError.grad(self, outputs, targets)` — Returns gradient of cross-entropy.
`CrossEntropySoftmaxError.__call__(self, outputs, targets)` — Returns scalar cross-entropy with numerically stable softmax.
`CrossEntropySoftmaxError.grad(self, outputs, targets)` — Returns gradient combining softmax and cross-entropy.
`BinaryCrossEntropySigmoidError.__call__(self, outputs, targets)` — Returns scalar binary cross-entropy with sigmoid applied to outputs.
`BinaryCrossEntropySigmoidError.grad(self, outputs, targets)` — Returns gradient of binary CE with sigmoid.

Learning rules (`mlp/learning_rules.py`):
`GradientDescentLearningRule.__init__(self, learning_rate=1e-3)` — Validates and stores the scalar learning rate.
`GradientDescentLearningRule.initialise(self, params)` — stores the parameter list for in-place updates.
`GradientDescentLearningRule.update_params(self, grads_wrt_params)` — vanilla gradient descent update over all stored parameters.
`MomentumLearningRule.__init__(self, learning_rate=1e-3, mom_coeff=0.9)` — Validates and stores momentum hyperparameters.
`MomentumLearningRule.initialise(self, params)` — stores params and initialises zero-valued momentum buffers.
`MomentumLearningRule.reset(self)` — Zeroes the accumulated momentum buffers.
`MomentumLearningRule.update_params(self, grads_wrt_params)` — Momentum SGD update using `self.mom_coeff` and accumulated momentum.
`RMSPropLearningRule.__init__(self, learning_rate=1e-3, beta=0.9, epsilon=1e-8)` — Validates and stores RMSProp hyperparameters.
`RMSPropLearningRule.initialise(self, params)` — stores the parameter list and initialises zero-valued `self.mssq` state arrays matching each parameter.
`RMSPropLearningRule.reset(self)` — resets `self.mssq` to zeros.
`RMSPropLearningRule.update_params(self, grads_wrt_params)` — RMSProp parameter update using `self.beta`, `self.epsilon`, and `self.mssq` state.
`AdamLearningRule.__init__(self, learning_rate=1e-3, beta1=0.9, beta2=0.999, epsilon=1e-8)` — Validates and stores Adam hyperparameters.
`AdamLearningRule.initialise(self, params)` — stores the parameter list and initialises zero-valued `self.ms`, `self.vs`, and `self.t` state.
`AdamLearningRule.reset(self)` — resets `self.ms`, `self.vs`, and `self.t` to their initial values.
`AdamLearningRule.update_params(self, grads_wrt_params)` — Adam parameter update using `self.beta1`, `self.beta2`, `self.epsilon`, `self.ms`, `self.vs`, and `self.t` state.

Models (`mlp/models.py`):
`SingleLayerModel.__init__(self, layer)` — Stores the wrapped layer for later proxying.
`SingleLayerModel.params` — proxies the wrapped layer parameter list.
`SingleLayerModel.fprop(self, inputs)` — returns `[inputs, layer_outputs]`.
`SingleLayerModel.grads_wrt_params(self, activations, grads_wrt_outputs)` — delegates parameter-gradient computation to the wrapped layer.
`MultipleLayerModel.__init__(self, layers)` — Stores the layer sequence in model order.
`MultipleLayerModel.params` — returns a flattened list of parameters from every parameterised layer in model order.
`MultipleLayerModel.fprop(self, inputs, evaluation=False)` — Forward propagates through all layers, returning list of all activations (including inputs).
`MultipleLayerModel.grads_wrt_params(self, activations, grads_wrt_outputs)` — Backpropagates through all layers, returning list of parameter gradients.

Optimisers (`mlp/optimisers.py`):
`Optimiser.__init__(self, model, error, learning_rule, train_dataset, valid_dataset=None, data_monitors=None, notebook=False)` — Wires together the model, error, datasets, and learning-rule state.
`Optimiser.do_training_epoch(self)` — Runs one full training epoch over the training dataset.
`Optimiser.eval_monitors(self, dataset, label)` — Evaluates the configured monitors in evaluation mode and averages them over dataset batches.
`Optimiser.get_epoch_stats(self)` — Returns aggregated train/valid monitor stats for the current epoch.
`Optimiser.log_stats(self, epoch, epoch_time, stats)` — Logs a formatted per-epoch summary.
`Optimiser.train(self, num_epochs, stats_interval=5)` — Runs the full training loop and returns recorded statistics and elapsed time.

69	
70	    Initialises an two-dimensional parameter array using the 'normalized
71	    initialisation' scheme suggested in [1] which attempts to maintain a
72	    roughly constant variance in the activations and backpropagated gradients
73	    of a multi-layer model consisting of interleaved affine and logistic
74	    sigmoidal transformation layers.
75	
76	    Weights are sampled from a zero-mean uniform distribution with standard
77	    deviation `sqrt(2 / (input_dim * output_dim))` where `input_dim` and
78	    `output_dim` are the input and output dimensions of the weight matrix
79	    respectively.
80	
81	    References:
82	      [1]: Understanding the difficulty of training deep feedforward neural
83	           networks, Glorot and Bengio (2010)
84	    """
85	
86	    def __init__(self, gain=1., rng=None):
87	        """Construct a normalised initilisation random initialiser object.
88	
89	        Args:
90	            gain: Multiplicative factor to scale initialised weights by.
91	                Recommended values is 1 for affine layers followed by
92	                logistic sigmoid layers (or another affine layer).
93	            rng (RandomState): Seeded random number generator.
94	        """
95	        self.gain = gain
96	        if rng is None:
97	            rng = np.random.RandomState(DEFAULT_SEED)
98	        self.rng = rng
99

101	        assert len(shape) == 2, (
102	            'Initialiser should only be used for two dimensional arrays.')
103	        std = self.gain * (2. / (shape[0] + shape[1]))**0.5
104	        half_width = 3.**0.5 * std
105	        return self.rng.uniform(low=-half_width, high=half_width, size=shape)

5	minimise the error function given a set of inputs and target outputs.

8	model outputs and target outputs, averaged over all data points in the data set
9	or batch.

15	class SumOfSquaredDiffsError(object):
16	    """Sum of squared differences (squared Euclidean distance) error."""
17	
18	    def __call__(self, outputs, targets):
19	        """Calculates error function given a batch of outputs and targets.
20	
21	        Args:
22	            outputs: Array of model outputs of shape (batch_size, output_dim).
23	            targets: Array of target outputs of shape (batch_size, output_dim).
24	
25	        Returns:
26	            Scalar cost function value.
27	        """
28	        return 0.5 * np.mean(np.sum((outputs - targets)**2, axis=1))
29	
30	    def grad(self, outputs, targets):
31	        """Calculates gradient of error function with respect to outputs.
32	
33	        Args:
34	            outputs: Array of model outputs of shape (batch_size, output_dim).
35	            targets: Array of target outputs of shape (batch_size, output_dim).
36	
37	        Returns:
38	            Gradient of error function with respect to outputs.
39	        """
40	        return (outputs - targets) / outputs.shape[0]
41

46	class BinaryCrossEntropyError(object):

49	    def __call__(self, outputs, targets):
50	        """Calculates error function given a batch of outputs and targets.
51	
52	        Args:
53	            outputs: Array of model outputs of shape (batch_size, output_dim).
54	            targets: Array of target outputs of shape (batch_size, output_dim).
55	
56	        Returns:
57	            Scalar error function value.
58	        """
59	        return -np.mean(
60	            targets * np.log(outputs) + (1. - targets) * np.log(1. - ouputs))
61	
62	    def grad(self, outputs, targets):
63	        """Calculates gradient of error function with respect to outputs.
64	
65	        Args:
66	            outputs: Array of model outputs of shape (batch_size, output_dim).
67	            targets: Array of target outputs of shape (batch_size, output_dim).
68	
69	        Returns:
70	            Gradient of error function with respect to outputs.
71	        """
72	        return ((1. - targets) / (1. - outputs) -
73	                (targets / outputs)) / outputs.shape[0]

101	            targets: Array of target outputs of shape (batch_size, output_dim).
102

152	            targets: Array of target outputs of shape (batch_size, output_dim).
153	
154	        Returns:
155	            Scalar error function value.

159	        return -np.mean(np.sum(targets * logProb, axis=1))

162	        """Calculates gradient of error function with respect to outputs.
163

165	            outputs: Array of model outputs of shape (batch_size, output_dim).
166	            targets: Array of target outputs of shape (batch_size, output_dim).
167	
168	        Returns:

170	        """

10	class GradientDescentLearningRule(object):
11	    """Simple (stochastic) gradient descent learning rule.
12	
13	    For a scalar error function `E(p[0], p_[1] ... )` of some set of
14	    potentially multidimensional parameters this attempts to find a local
15	    minimum of the loss function by applying updates to each parameter of the
16	    form
17	
18	        p[i] := p[i] - learning_rate * dE/dp[i]
19	
20	    With `learning_rate` a positive scaling parameter.
21	
22	    The error function used in successive applications of these updates may be
23	    a stochastic estimator of the true error function (e.g. when the error with
24	    respect to only a subset of data-points is calculated) in which case this
25	    will correspond to a stochastic gradient descent learning rule.
26	    """
27	
28	    def __init__(self, learning_rate=1e-3):
29	        """Creates a new learning rule object.
30	
31	        Args:
32	            learning_rate: A postive scalar to scale gradient updates to the
33	                parameters by. This needs to be carefully set - if too large
34	                the learning dynamic will be unstable and may diverge, while
35	                if set too small learning will proceed very slowly.
36	
37	        """
38	        assert learning_rate > 0., 'learning_rate should be positive.'
39	        self.learning_rate = learning_rate
40	
41	    def initialise(self, params):
42	        """Initialises the state of the learning rule for a set or parameters.
43	
44	        This must be called before `update_params` is first called.
45	
46	        Args:
47	            params: A list of the parameters to be optimised. Note these will
48	                be updated *in-place* to avoid reallocating arrays on each
49	                update.
50	        """
51	        self.params = params
52	
53	    def reset(self):
54	        """Resets any additional state variables to their intial values.
55	
56	        For this learning rule there are no additional state variables so we
57	        do nothing here.
58	        """
59	        pass
60	
61	    def update_params(self, grads_wrt_params):
62	        """Applies a single gradient descent update to all parameters.
63	
64	        All parameter updates are performed using in-place operations and so
65	        nothing is returned.
66	
67	        Args:
68	            grads_wrt_params: A list of gradients of the scalar loss function
69	                with respect to each of the parameters passed to `initialise`
70	                previously, with this list expected to be in the same order.
71	        """
72	        for param, grad in zip(self.params, grads_wrt_params):
73	            param -= self.learning_rate * grad

77	    """Gradient descent with momentum learning rule.

80	    momentum state variables for each parameter. These can help the learning

85	    scalar loss function `L` are of the form

88	        p[i] := p[i] + m[i]

95	    def __init__(self, learning_rate=1e-3, mom_coeff=0.9):

102	                if set too small learning will proceed very slowly.

104	                the contribution of the previous momentum value to the value

190	                estimates. This should be a scalar value in [0, 1]. The run

196	                second moment estimates are close to zero. Should be set to
197	                a small positive value.

200	        assert beta_1 >= 0. and beta_1 <= 1., 'beta_1 should be in [0, 1].'

202	        assert epsilon > 0., 'epsilon should be > 0.'

204	        self.beta_2 = beta_2
205	        self.epsilon = epsilon

207	    def initialise(self, params):

210	        Args:
211	            params: A list of the parameters to be optimised. Note these will
212	                be updated *in-place* to avoid reallocating arrays on each
213	                update.
214	        """
215	        super(AdamLearningRule, self).initialise(params)
216	        self.moms_1 = []
217	        for param in self.params:
218	            self.moms_1.append(np.zeros_like(param))
219	        self.moms_2 = []
220	        for param in self.params:

222	        self.step_count = 0

229	        for mom_1, mom_2 in zip(self.moms_1, self.moms_2):
230	            mom_1 *= 0.
231	            mom_2 *= 0.
232	        self.step_count = 0

279	        assert epsilon > 0., 'epsilon should be > 0.'
280	        self.epsilon = epsilon

290	        super(AdaGradLearningRule, self).initialise(params)
291	        self.sum_sq_grads = []
292	        for param in self.params:
293	            self.sum_sq_grads.append(np.zeros_like(param))

295	    def reset(self):
296	        """Resets any additional state variables to their initial values.
297	        For this learning rule this corresponds to zeroing all the sum of

364	            self.moms_2.append(np.zeros_like(param))

    """Layer implementing projection to a grid of radial basis functions."""

    def __init__(self, grid_dim, intervals=[[0., 1.]]):
        """Creates a radial basis function layer object.

        self.centres = np.array(np.meshgrid(*[
            np.linspace(low, high, grid_dim) for (low, high) in intervals])
        ).reshape((len(intervals), -1))

            [(high - low) * 1. / grid_dim] for (low, high) in intervals])

        """Forward propagates activations through the layer transformation.

# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""Error functions.

This module defines error functions, with the aim of model training being to
minimise the error function given a set of inputs and target outputs.

The error functions will typically measure some concept of distance between the
model outputs and target outputs, averaged over all data points in the data set
or batch.
"""

import numpy as np


class SumOfSquaredDiffsError(object):
    """Sum of squared differences (squared Euclidean distance) error."""

    def __call__(self, outputs, targets):
        """Calculates error function given a batch of outputs and targets.

        Args:
            outputs: Array of model outputs of shape (batch_size, output_dim).
            targets: Array of target outputs of shape (batch_size, output_dim).

        Returns:
            Scalar cost function value.
        """
        return 0.5 * np.mean(np.sum((outputs - targets)**2, axis=1))

    def grad(self, outputs, targets):
        """Calculates gradient of error function with respect to outputs.

        Args:
            outputs: Array of model outputs of shape (batch_size, output_dim).
            targets: Array of target outputs of shape (batch_size, output_dim).

        Returns:
            Gradient of error function with respect to outputs.
        """
        return (outputs - targets) / outputs.shape[0]

    def __repr__(self):
        return 'MeanSquaredErrorCost'


class BinaryCrossEntropyError(object):
    """Binary cross entropy error."""

    def __call__(self, outputs, targets):
        """Calculates error function given a batch of outputs and targets.

        Args:
            outputs: Array of model outputs of shape (batch_size, output_dim).
            targets: Array of target outputs of shape (batch_size, output_dim).

        Returns:
            Scalar error function value.
        """
        return -np.mean(
            targets * np.log(outputs) + (1. - targets) * np.log(1. - outputs))

    def grad(self, outputs, targets):
        """Calculates gradient of error function with respect to outputs.

        Args:
            outputs: Array of model outputs of shape (batch_size, output_dim).
            targets: Array of target outputs of shape (batch_size, output_dim).

        Returns:
            Gradient of error function with respect to outputs.
        """
        return ((1. - targets) / (1. - outputs) -
                (targets / outputs)) / outputs.shape[0]

    def __repr__(self):
        return 'BinaryCrossEntropyError'


class BinaryCrossEntropySigmoidError(object):
    """Binary cross entropy error with logistic sigmoid applied to outputs."""

    def __call__(self, outputs, targets):
        """Calculates error function given a batch of outputs and targets.

        Args:
            outputs: Array of model outputs of shape (batch_size, output_dim).
            targets: Array of target outputs of shape (batch_size, output_dim).

        Returns:
            Scalar error function value.
        """
        probs = 1. / (1. + np.exp(-outputs))
        return -np.mean(
            targets * np.log(probs) + (1. - targets) * np.log(1. - probs))

    def grad(self, outputs, targets):
        """Calculates gradient of error function with respect to outputs.

        Args:
            outputs: Array of model outputs of shape (batch_size, output_dim).
            targets: Array of target outputs of shape (batch_size, output_dim).

        Returns:
            Gradient of error function with respect to outputs.
        """
        probs = 1. / (1. + np.exp(-outputs))
        return (probs - targets) / outputs.shape[0]

    def __repr__(self):
        return 'BinaryCrossEntropySigmoidError'


class CrossEntropyError(object):
    """Multi-class cross entropy error."""

    def __call__(self, outputs, targets):
        """Calculates error function given a batch of outputs and targets.

        Args:
            outputs: Array of model outputs of shape (batch_size, output_dim).
            targets: Array of target outputs of shape (batch_size, output_dim).

        Returns:
            Scalar error function value.
        """
        return -np.mean(np.sum(targets * np.log(outputs), axis=1))

    def grad(self, outputs, targets):
        """Calculates gradient of error function with respect to outputs.

        Args:
            outputs: Array of model outputs of shape (batch_size, output_dim).
            targets: Array of target outputs of shape (batch_size, output_dim).

        Returns:
            Gradient of error function with respect to outputs.
        """
        return -(targets / outputs) / outputs.shape[0]

    def __repr__(self):
        return 'CrossEntropyError'


class CrossEntropySoftmaxError(object):
    """Multi-class cross entropy error with Softmax applied to outputs."""

    def __call__(self, outputs, targets):
        """Calculates error function given a batch of outputs and targets.

        Args:
            outputs: Array of model outputs of shape (batch_size, output_dim).
            targets: Array of target outputs of shape (batch_size, output_dim).

        Returns:
            Scalar error function value.
        """
        normOutputs = outputs - outputs.max(-1)[:, None]
        logProb = normOutputs - np.log(np.sum(np.exp(normOutputs), axis=-1)[:, None])
        return -np.mean(np.sum(targets * logProb, axis=1))

    def grad(self, outputs, targets):
        """Calculates gradient of error function with respect to outputs.

        Args:
            outputs: Array of model outputs of shape (batch_size, output_dim).
            targets: Array of target outputs of shape (batch_size, output_dim).

        Returns:
            Gradient of error function with respect to outputs.
        """
        probs = np.exp(outputs - outputs.max(-1)[:, None])
        probs /= probs.sum(-1)[:, None]
        return (probs - targets) / outputs.shape[0]

    def __repr__(self):
        return 'CrossEntropySoftmaxError'

        assert beta2 >= 0. and beta2 <= 1., 'beta2 should be in [0, 1].'

        self.beta2 = beta2

                update.

        for param in self.params:
            self.ms.append(np.zeros_like(param))
        self.vs = []
        for param in self.params:

        For this learning rule this corresponds to zeroing the first and
        second moment estimates and resetting the time step counter.

        second moment estimates and resetting the time step counter.

class LeakyReluLayer(Layer):
    """Layer implementing an element-wise leaky rectified linear transformation."""
    def __init__(self, alpha=0.01):
        self.alpha = alpha

    def fprop(self, inputs):
        """Forward propagates activations through the layer transformation.

        For inputs `x` and outputs `y` this corresponds to
        `y = x` for positive `x` and `y = alpha * x` for negative `x`.
        """
        return np.where(inputs > 0, inputs, self.alpha * inputs)

        """Back propagates gradients through a layer.

        Given gradients with respect to the outputs of the layer calculates the
        gradients with respect to the layer inputs.

import numpy as np
from mlp import layers

rng = np.random.RandomState(2312)

def num_grad_inputs(layer, x, eps=1e-6):
    g = np.zeros_like(x)
    it = np.nditer(x, flags=['multi_index'])
    while not it.finished:
        i = it.multi_index
        old = x[i]
        x[i] = old + eps; fp = layer.fprop(x)
        x[i] = old - eps; fm = layer.fprop(x)
        x[i] = old
        # use random projection scalar function: sum(outputs * w)
        g[i] = ((fp - fm) * w).sum() / (2*eps)
        it.iternext()
    return g

x = rng.normal(size=(4, 5))
g_out = rng.normal(size=(4, 3))

for name, layer, xx in [
    ('Affine', layers.AffineLayer(5, 3), x),
    ('Sigmoid', layers.SigmoidLayer(), x),
    ('Relu', layers.ReluLayer(), x),
    ('LeakyRelu', layers.LeakyReluLayer(0.1), x),
    ('ELU', layers.ELULayer(0.8), x),
    ('Tanh', layers.TanhLayer(), x),
    ('Softmax', layers.SoftmaxLayer(), x),
    ('Reshape', layers.ReshapeLayer(), x),
]:
    outs = layer.fprop(xx)
    w = rng.normal(size=outs.shape)
    analytic = layer.bprop(xx, outs, w)
    numeric = num_grad_inputs(layer, xx.copy())
    print(name, 'bprop OK' if np.allclose(analytic, numeric, atol=1e-5) else 'bprop MISMATCH')

# affine grads_wrt_params numerical check
layer = layers.AffineLayer(5, 3)
outs = layer.fprop(x)
w = rng.normal(size=outs.shape)
def scalar_fn():
    return (layer.fprop(x) * w).sum()
for pi, param in enumerate(layer.params):
    num = np.zeros_like(param)
    it = np.nditer(param, flags=['multi_index'])
    while not it.finished:
        i = it.multi_index; old = param[i]
        param[i] = old + 1e-6; fp = scalar_fn()
        param[i] = old - 1e-6; fm = scalar_fn()
        param[i] = old
        num[i] = (fp - fm) / 2e-6
        it.iternext()
    analytic = layer.grads_wrt_params(x, w)[pi]
    print('Affine param', pi, 'OK' if np.allclose(analytic, num, atol=1e-4) else 'MISMATCH')

# params getter/setter
layer2 = layers.AffineLayer(5, 3)
layer2.params = layer.params
assert all(np.shares_memory(a, b) or np.array_equal(a, b) for a, b in zip(layer2.params, layer.params))
assert layer2.params_penalty() == 0
assert layer.params_penalty() == 0

# penalty support
class L2:
    def __call__(self, p): return 0.5 * (p**2).sum()
    def grad(self, p): return p
layer3 = layers.AffineLayer(5, 3, weights_penalty=L2(), biases_penalty=L2())
p = layer3.params_penalty()
g = layer3.grads_wrt_params(x, w)
assert np.isscalar(p) or p.ndim == 0
assert np.allclose(g[0], np.dot(w.T, x) + layer3.weights)
print('Affine penalty OK')

# RBF checks: fprop shape and bprop numerical
rbf = layers.RadialBasisFunctionLayer(4, intervals=[[0., 1.], [-1., 1.]])
xr = rng.uniform(0, 1, size=(3, 2))
outs = rbf.fprop(xr)
print('RBF out shape', outs.shape, '(expect (3, 8))')
w = rng.normal(size=outs.shape)
analytic = rbf.bprop(xr, outs, w)
numeric = num_grad_inputs(rbf, xr.copy())
print('RBF bprop', 'OK' if np.allclose(analytic, numeric, atol=1e-5) else 'MISMATCH')
print('RBF repr:', repr(rbf))

# Dropout checks
dr = layers.DropoutLayer(rng=np.random.RandomState(42), incl_prob=0.7, share_across_batch=True)
xx = rng.normal(size=(6, 4))
o1 = dr.fprop(xx, stochastic=True)
assert dr._mask.shape == (1, 4)
assert np.array_equal(o1, xx * dr._mask)
assert np.array_equal(dr.bprop(xx, o1, xx), xx * dr._mask)
odet = dr.fprop(xx, stochastic=False)
assert np.allclose(odet, xx * 0.7)
dr2 = layers.DropoutLayer(rng=np.random.RandomState(42), incl_prob=0.5, share_across_batch=False)
o2 = dr2.fprop(xx)
assert dr2._mask.shape == xx.shape
try:
    layers.DropoutLayer(incl_prob=0.)
    raise SystemExit('no assert')
except AssertionError: pass
print('Dropout OK')

# Reshape explicit shape
rs = layers.ReshapeLayer((2, 2))
xx = rng.normal(size=(3, 4))
oo = rs.fprop(xx)
assert oo.shape == (3, 2, 2)
assert np.array_equal(rs.bprop(xx, oo, oo).shape, xx.shape)
rs2 = layers.ReshapeLayer()
assert rs2.fprop(oo).shape == (3, 4)
print('Reshape OK')
EOF

                    grads_wrt_outputs[:, :, i, j], kernels, axes=([1], [0]))

    def grads_wrt_params(self, inputs, grads_wrt_outputs):
        """Calculates gradients with respect to layer parameters.
        Args:
            inputs: array of inputs to layer of shape (batch_size, input_dim)
            grads_wrt_to_outputs: array of gradients with respect to the layer
                outputs of shape
                (batch_size, num_output-_channels, output_dim_1, output_dim_2).
        Returns:
            list of arrays of gradients with respect to the layer parameters
            `[grads_wrt_kernels, grads_wrt_biases]`.
        """
        output_dim_1 = self.input_dim_1 - self.kernel_dim_1 + 1
        output_dim_2 = self.input_dim_2 - self.kernel_dim_2 + 1
        grads_wrt_kernels = np.zeros(self.kernels_shape, dtype=np.float64)
        for i in range(output_dim_1):
            for j in range(output_dim_2):
                window = inputs[:, :, i:i + self.kernel_dim_1,
                                j:j + self.kernel_dim_2]
                grads_wrt_kernels += np.tensordot(
                    grads_wrt_outputs[:, :, i, j], window, axes=([0], [0]))

        grads_wrt_kernels = grads_wrt_kernels[:, :, ::-1, ::-1]
        grads_wrt_biases = grads_wrt_outputs.sum(axis=(0, 2, 3))

        if self.kernels_penalty is not None:
            grads_wrt_kernels += self.kernels_penalty.grad(self.kernels)
        if self.biases_penalty is not None:
            grads_wrt_biases += self.biases_penalty.grad(self.biases)

        return [grads_wrt_kernels, grads_wrt_biases]

    def params_penalty(self):
        """Returns the parameter dependent penalty term for this layer.
        If no parameter-dependent penalty terms are set this returns zero.
        """

        if self.kernels_penalty is not None:
            params_penalty += self.kernels_penalty(self.kernels)
        if self.biases_penalty is not None:
            params_penalty += self.biases_penalty(self.biases)
        return params_penalty

    def params(self):
        """A list of layer parameter values: `[kernels, biases]`."""
        return [self.kernels, self.biases]

    def params(self, values):
        self.kernels = values[0]
        self.biases = values[1]

# wrt params
for pi, param in enumerate(layer.params):
    num = np.zeros_like(param, dtype=float)
    it = np.nditer(param, flags=['multi_index'])
    while not it.finished:
        i = it.multi_index; old = param[i]
        param[i] = old + eps; fp = (layer.fprop(x) * w).sum()
        param[i] = old - eps; fm = (layer.fprop(x) * w).sum()

    i = it.multi_index; old = xb[i]
    xb[i] = old + eps; fp = (bn.fprop(xb) * wb).sum()
    xb[i] = old - eps; fm = (bn.fprop(xb) * wb).sum()
    xb[i] = old
    gb[i] = (fp - fm) / (2*eps); it.iternext()

od = bn.fprop(xb, stochastic=False)

print('BN deterministic mode OK')
EOF

import numpy as np
from mlp.layers import (AffineLayer, SigmoidLayer, ReluLayer, DropoutLayer,
                        BatchNormalizationLayer, ReshapeLayer)
from mlp.models import SingleLayerModel, MultipleLayerModel
from mlp.errors import CrossEntropySoftmaxError
from mlp.initialisers import UniformInit, ConstantInit

rng = np.random.RandomState(99)
x = rng.normal(size=(4, 6))

# SingleLayerModel
layer = AffineLayer(6, 3)
m = SingleLayerModel(layer)
assert m.params is layer.params or m.params == layer.params
acts = m.fprop(x)
assert len(acts) == 2 and np.array_equal(acts[0], x) and np.array_equal(acts[1], layer.fprop(x))
g = rng.normal(size=(4, 3))
assert all(np.array_equal(a, b) for a, b in zip(
    m.grads_wrt_params(acts, g), layer.grads_wrt_params(x, g)))
print('SingleLayerModel OK', repr(m))

# MultipleLayerModel params flattening (skip non-parameterised layers)
model = MultipleLayerModel([
    AffineLayer(6, 5), ReluLayer(), AffineLayer(5, 3), SigmoidLayer()])
assert len(model.params) == 4  # W1,b1,W2,b2
acts = model.fprop(x)
assert len(acts) == 5
# end-to-end gradient check through model with error
error = CrossEntropySoftmaxError()
t = np.eye(3)[[0, 1, 2, 0]]
g_out = error.grad(acts[-1], t)
gparams = model.grads_wrt_params(acts, g_out)
assert len(gparams) == 4

def loss():
    return error(model.fprop(x)[-1], t)
eps = 1e-6
for p, gp in zip(model.params, gparams):
    num = np.zeros_like(p)
    it = np.nditer(p, flags=['multi_index'])
    while not it.finished:
        i = it.multi_index; old = p[i]
        p[i] = old + eps; fp = loss()
        p[i] = old - eps; fm = loss()
        p[i] = old
        num[i] = (fp - fm) / (2 * eps)
        it.iternext()
    assert np.allclose(gp, num, atol=1e-4), np.abs(gp - num).max()
print('MultipleLayerModel grads OK')

# evaluation flag with stochastic layers
model2 = MultipleLayerModel([
    AffineLayer(6, 5), DropoutLayer(rng=np.random.RandomState(1), incl_prob=0.5),
    BatchNormalizationLayer(5), AffineLayer(5, 3)])
a_train = model2.fprop(x)
a_eval = model2.fprop(x, evaluation=True)
assert len(a_train) == 5 and len(a_eval) == 5
# deterministic eval: dropout scales by incl_prob

a_train2 = model2.fprop(x)

assert len(gps) == 6  # W,b,gamma,beta,W,b
print('MultipleLayerModel stochastic OK', repr(model2).splitlines()[0])

        self.notebook = notebook

            self.tqdm_progress = getattr(tqdm, 'tqdm_notebook', tqdm.tqdm)
        else:
            self.tqdm_progress = tqdm.tqdm

    def do_training_epoch(self):
        """Do a single training epoch.

        This iterates through all batches in training dataset, for each
        calculating the gradient of the estimated error given the batch with
        respect to all the model parameters and then updates the model
        parameters according to the learning rule.
        """
        with self.tqdm_progress(
                total=self.train_dataset.num_batches) as train_progress_bar:
            train_progress_bar.set_description("Epoch Progress")
            for inputs_batch, targets_batch in self.train_dataset:
                activations = self.model.fprop(inputs_batch)
                grads_wrt_outputs = self.error.grad(
                    activations[-1], targets_batch)
                grads_wrt_params = self.model.grads_wrt_params(
                    activations, grads_wrt_outputs)
                self.learning_rule.update_params(grads_wrt_params)
                train_progress_bar.update(1)

    def eval_monitors(self, dataset, label):
        """Evaluates the monitors for the given dataset.

        Args:
            dataset: Dataset to perform evaluation with.
            label: Tag to add to end of monitor keys to identify dataset.

        Returns:
            OrderedDict of monitor values evaluated on dataset.
        """
        data_mon_vals = OrderedDict([(key + label, 0.) for key
                                     in self.data_monitors.keys()])
        for inputs_batch, targets_batch in dataset:
            activations = self.model.fprop(inputs_batch, evaluation=True)
            for key, data_monitor in self.data_monitors.items():
                data_mon_vals[key + label] += data_monitor(
                    activations[-1], targets_batch)
        for key, data_monitor in self.data_monitors.items():
            data_mon_vals[key + label] /= dataset.num_batches
        return data_mon_vals

    def get_epoch_stats(self):
        """Computes training statistics for an epoch.

        Returns:
            An OrderedDict with keys corresponding to the statistic labels and
            values corresponding to the value of the statistic.
        """
        epoch_stats = OrderedDict()
        epoch_stats.update(self.eval_monitors(self.train_dataset, '(train)'))
        if self.valid_dataset is not None:
            epoch_stats.update(self.eval_monitors(
                self.valid_dataset, '(valid)'))
        return epoch_stats

    def log_stats(self, epoch, epoch_time, stats):
        """Outputs stats for a training epoch to a logger.

        Args:
            epoch (int): Epoch counter.
            epoch_time: Time taken in seconds for the epoch to complete.
            stats: Monitored stats for the epoch.
        """
        logger.info('Epoch {0}: {1:.1f}s to complete\n    {2}'.format(
            epoch, epoch_time,
            ', '.join(['{0}={1:.2e}'.format(k, v) for (k, v) in stats.items()])
        ))

    def train(self, num_epochs, stats_interval=5):
        """Trains a model for a set number of epochs.

        Args:
            num_epochs: Number of epochs (complete passes through trainin
                dataset) to train for.
            stats_interval: Training statistics will be recorded and logged
                every `stats_interval` epochs.

        Returns:
            Tuple with first value being an array of training run statistics
            and the second being a dict mapping the labels for the statistics
            recorded to their column index in the array.
        """
        start_train_time = time.time()
        initial_stats = self.get_epoch_stats()
        run_stats = [list(initial_stats.values())]
        stat_keys = list(initial_stats.keys())
        with self.tqdm_progress(total=num_epochs) as progress_bar:
            progress_bar.set_description("Experiment Progress")
            for epoch in range(1, num_epochs + 1):
                start_time = time.time()
                self.do_training_epoch()
                epoch_time = time.time() - start_time
                if epoch % stats_interval == 0:
                    stats = self.get_epoch_stats()
                    self.log_stats(epoch, epoch_time, stats)
                    run_stats.append(list(stats.values()))
                progress_bar.update(1)
        finish_train_time = time.time()
        total_train_time = finish_train_time - start_train_time
        return (np.array(run_stats),
                {k: i for i, k in enumerate(stat_keys)},
                total_train_time)

            epoch_stats.update(self.eval_monitors(
                self.valid_dataset, '(valid)'))
        return epoch_stats

    def log_stats(self, epoch, epoch_time, stats):
        """Outputs stats for a training epoch to a logger.

        Args:
            epoch (int): Epoch counter.
            epoch_time: Time taken in seconds for the epoch to complete.
            stats: Monitored stats for the epoch.
        """
        logger.info('Epoch {0}: {1:.1f}s to complete\n    {2}'.format(
            epoch, epoch_time,
            ', '.join(['{0}={1:.2e}'.format(k, v) for (k, v) in stats.items()])
        ))

    def train(self, num_epochs, stats_interval=5):
        """Trains a model for a set number of epochs.

        Args:
            num_epochs: Number of epochs (complete passes through trainin
                dataset) to train for.
            stats_interval: Training statistics will be recorded and logged
                every `stats_interval` epochs.

        Returns:
            Tuple with first value being an array of training run statistics
            and the second being a dict mapping the labels for the statistics
            recorded to their column index in the array.
        """
        start_train_time = time.time()
        initial_stats = self.get_epoch_stats()
        run_stats = [list(initial_stats.values())]
        stat_keys = list(initial_stats.keys())
        with self.tqdm_progress(total=num_epochs) as progress_bar:
            progress_bar.set_description("Experiment Progress")
            for epoch in range(1, num_epochs + 1):
                start_time = time.time()
                self.do_training_epoch()
                epoch_time = time.time() - start_time
                if epoch % stats_interval == 0:
                    stats = self.get_epoch_stats()
                    self.log_stats(epoch, epoch_time, stats)
                    run_stats.append(list(stats.values()))
                progress_bar.update(1)
        finish_train_time = time.time()
        total_train_time = finish_train_time - start_train_time
        return (np.array(run_stats),
                {k: i for i, k in enumerate(stat_keys)},
                total_train_time)

# consolidated regression check across all implemented modules
from mlp import errors, layers, learning_rules, models, optimisers

rng = np.random.RandomState(2024)

    assert cond, name
    print('%-55s OK' % name)
